entries.name: context-property-calls-spend-i-eq-t3#0
entries.description: [I=] `sigmaProp(CONTEXT.INPUTS == INPUTS)`, tree v3, guards input 1 (SELF, value 1234567890) of two, three outputs, at height 1051200. THE CALL IS THE NODE: the property call returns the node's value, so the script reduces to true and the box SPENDS. An evaluator with no evaluator for the id refuses it.

entries.name: context-property-calls-spend-i2-t3#1
entries.description: [I2] `sigmaProp(CONTEXT.INPUTS.size == 2)`, tree v3, guards input 1 (SELF, value 1234567890) of two, three outputs, at height 1051200. The call against the TRUE value in this context, so a wired-but-wrong field is caught.

entries.name: context-property-calls-spend-i3-sep-t3#2
entries.description: [I3!] `sigmaProp(CONTEXT.INPUTS.size == 3)`, tree v3, guards input 1 (SELF, value 1234567890) of two, three outputs, at height 1051200. **THE SEPARATING ROW.** INVALID on the JVM: the property call returns the node's value, so `p` is false. 3 is the OUTPUTS count, so an evaluator wired that way makes `p` true and lets a spender TAKE a box anyone can create: an over-accept on reachable state.
